newsitem.title: UK: Pound hits UK car part sales to VW - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pound hits UK car part sales to VW - paper.

text.p: The UK motor components industry is losing millions of pounds in potential business from Volkswagen AG because sterling's strength is making British products uncompetitive, the Financial Times said on Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted a senior purchasing executive at the German carmaker as saying the group's target to triple purchases of car parts from the UK to 1.5 billion pounds ($2.43 billion) a year by 1999 would be harder to achieve if the pound stayed at current levels.

Mr Frans Boot, head of VW's UK purchasing, said spending on British car parts was likely to increase to about 600 million pounds ($971.9 million) this year compared with 550 million pounds ($890.9 million) in 1996. ($1=.6173 Pound)
